title: fix(app-shell): object list pages and their breadcrumb read the plural label (objectui#11696)
body:
Fixes #11696

Clause-②: yes

## What changed

Object list pages, and the breadcrumb segment that links to them, read the object's plural label. The record page keeps the singular.

- `@object-ui/i18n`: `useObjectLabel()` gains `objectPluralLabel(objectDef)` beside `objectLabel`. It returns the translated plural (`{ns}.objects.{objectName}.pluralLabel`), else the declared `objectDef.pluralLabel`, else the singular as `objectLabel` resolves it. An object that declares no plural keeps its label.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` `ObjectView`: the list page's `PageHeader` title uses it. That is the only line changed in this file besides the hook destructure.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` `ObjectDataPage`: the `/data` page (the URL-defined data slice badged "Data") lists the object's records under the same object crumb, so its `PageHeader` title uses it too. Only the title span and the hook destructure changed; the record drawer it opens keeps the singular.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` `AppHeader`: the object breadcrumb segment, its "Switch Object" entries, and the object crumbs of a record's ancestor trail use it.
- Untouched, still singular: the record page, the record drawer title (in `ObjectView` and in `ObjectDataPage`), the import wizard's object name, the favorite entry, "New" actions, and the record form page's own breadcrumb link (see Acceptance notes).

## Where it landed, and why that is not only where the card pointed

The claim's file surface named `ObjectView.tsx` for both the title and the breadcrumb. Read on `origin/main` at `7300fca`:

- The list title is the `PageHeader` in `ObjectView`. Changed.
- The "Project ▾" breadcrumb is not in `ObjectView`. `AppHeader` builds it: it is the object segment, and the ▾ is that segment's "Switch Object" dropdown. Changed there. This is the same package, and `AppHeader` is where the crumb is produced.
- The two `ObjectView` sites named in hypothesis 1 of the dispatch (`viewOriginLabel(…) || objectLabel(objectDef)`) build `location.state.from.label`. That is the record page's link back to the list, not the list title or the breadcrumb. Not changed, because it is a record-page surface. It is listed under Acceptance notes.

The object crumb is the same element on every route under the object (list, view, record), and it always links to the list. It reads the plural on all of those routes, so it does not change its own name when the trail continues into a record ("Projects › Apollo"). The alternative was a crumb that depends on the route. That would show "Projects ▾" on the list and "Project ▾" one click later, on the same link.

Overlap: seat 1's objectui#11685 may edit `ObjectView.tsx` in the record drawer's chrome. This PR touches that file only at the hook destructure and the list `PageHeader` title span. Whichever PR lands later merges the other.

## The nav entry

The sidebar entry "Projects" in the card takes its text from its own authored `label` (showcase `nav_projects`, Setup `nav_users`), not from object metadata. There is no shared source to reuse, and after this PR both read the plural. Measured once at objectstack `6befe19c`: every first-party `object` nav entry in objectstack's examples, platform objects and plugins carries a `label`, and so do both entries in objectui's examples. A nav entry with no label inherits its text through `useNavTargetLabel`, which calls `objectLabel`. That follows step 3 of the spec's nav-label rule ("the object's / dashboard's label"). It is not changed here: an object entry inheriting the plural is a reading of the spec contract, and it goes back to the PM as an open question.

## Judgment: a bundle that translates the singular but not the plural

This answers the question the dispatch left open in Zone 3. When the bundle has no `pluralLabel` but the object declares one, `objectPluralLabel` does not fall back to the translated singular. It shows the declared plural. The reason: `translateObject` in `@objectstack/spec` serves `pluralLabel` from `/meta` as the catalog entry, else the authored value, and has no step down to the translated singular. So this matches what every other consumer shows. A client-only step would be the second dialect that the `viewSuffixes` docblock already refuses. Exposure, measured once at objectstack `6befe19c`: the platform zh-CN object bundle carries `pluralLabel` for every object it translates, and so does every showcase object with a zh-CN entry. `os i18n extract` writes `pluralLabel` wherever an object declares one, so a missing plural is a gap in the bundle and gets fixed there.

## Tests

Three new pins, each named after this issue:

- `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/useObjectLabel-pluralLabel-11696.test.tsx` covers the resolution order. Cases: en declared plural; zh-CN translated plural over the declared one; a namespaced object resolved by its short name; singular fallback, translated and untranslated; an empty declared plural; and the Zone 3 case above.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.listTitlePlural-11696.test.tsx` mounts a real `ObjectView` inside a real i18next instance. "Projects" titles the projects list in en, the translated plural titles it in zh-CN, and an object with no plural is titled with its label.
- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/AppHeader.objectCrumbPlural-11696.test.tsx` uses the `AppHeader.servedLabels-11295` harness with the real `useObjectLabel`. It checks the list crumb in en and zh-CN, the "Switch Object" siblings (plural, falling back to the singular), the crumb staying plural on a record route, and a control.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectDataPage.listTitlePlural-11696.test.tsx` mounts a real `ObjectDataPage` inside a real i18next instance (the `ObjectDataPage.filterChipI18n-9159` mocks). "Projects" titles the projects `/data` page in en, the translated plural titles it in zh-CN, and an object with no plural is titled with its label. It reads the title's own `span.truncate`, because the heading also holds the "Data" badge.

In the zh-CN fixtures `pluralLabel` differs from `label` on purpose. Shipped zh-CN bundles often use one word for both (`项目` / `项目`), and with equal strings an assertion cannot tell which key was read.

One existing pin moved: `useObjectLabel-identity-5564` anchors the hook's member count to an absolute number, and a new resolver changes it (27 to 28), as objectui#11344 did before.

## Reverse verification (on `29cba5f`, the implementation commit)

The mutation, applied after the fix was committed: in `AppHeader`, the hook destructure was changed to alias `objectLabel` as `objectPluralLabel`, so every object crumb reads the singular. In `ObjectView`, the title span was put back to `objectLabel(objectDef)`. Both edits went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each anchor hit exactly once and each file's blob changed. The restore was proven by the blob matching `HEAD` and by an empty `git diff HEAD`, not by an exit code.

- **Predicted before the run:** `AppHeader` 4 red and 1 green (the control); `ObjectView` 2 red and 1 green (the control).
- **Observed:** `Tests 6 failed | 2 passed (8)`. The failures read `expected 'Project' to be 'Projects'`, `expected '项目' to be '项目清单'`, `expected [ 'Task' ] to deeply equal [ 'Tasks' ]`, and the crumb text not found. Both controls stayed green.

Blind spot: a test that renders these components through a component whose name matches none of those words.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed; no carrier)

- **Label-less `object` nav entries inherit the singular** (`useNavTargetLabel` calls `objectLabel`), following step 3 of the spec ("the object's / dashboard's label"). After this PR such an entry would read "Project" next to a "Projects" title. No first-party producer writes one (measured above). The objectstack CLI scaffolder already writes the plural as a nav entry's label (`objectPluralLabel` in `generate.ts`). The seat answered A: no change here. If it is ever pulled, the spec amends step 3 first and objectui follows.
- **The record page's back-link** (`viewOriginLabel(…) || objectLabel(objectDef)` in `ObjectView`) names the list with the singular when the active view has no label. It is a record-page surface, so it is left alone.
- **Related-list titles on the record page** (`RecordDetailView`'s related lists, and the fallback in `record-related-list.tsx`) title a list of child records with the child object's singular label. This is the same family as this card and was not touched.
- **Favorites and recent items** label an object-list entry with the singular (`ObjectView`'s favorite toggle; the `object` kind in `useRecentItemLabel` through `useNavTargetLabel`). Same family, not touched.
- **The record form page's own breadcrumb** (`RecordFormPage`) links to the object list with the singular `label` that it shares with its "New …" / "Edit …" title, under the `AppHeader` crumb that now reads the plural. It is a record-scoped page, so it is left alone; changing it means splitting that shared variable.
- **Client bundle over a served label.** `objectLabel`, and `objectPluralLabel` because it mirrors it, consult the client bundle before the served value. The server lets a tenant's explicit override beat the catalog (the objectstack#8284 ruling), and objectui#11295 already made views and dashboards draw a served label as given. Whether an object rename shows in the console was not measured. This is a read-only inference.
